entries.name: CIMAT Guanajuato
entries.upstream: Authorized institutional account; public Slurm manual
entries.reuse: Use the account's available submission mechanism, and the site's allocation, storage and identity rules.
entries.build: Add a local connection profile with capability discovery. Choose the bounded SSH worker or the supported queue after checking the assigned host. Keep credentials and site-specific paths outside this repository.
entries.test: Check account capabilities and scratch read/write with synthetic data. Run a fixed CPU fixture natively and through MCP, then transfer a public Guanajuato tile package and verify the output in OLDT. Record the available queue and actual consumption.

entries.name: Managed Python environment over SSH
entries.upstream: Python venv and pip wheel locks, executed through the authorized OpenSSH profile
entries.reuse: Use the existing SSH launcher, trusted workspace manifests and verified job receipts.
entries.build: Inspect visible resources and command availability. Prepare a pinned user environment and run a bounded batch with that interpreter.
entries.test: Start with a fresh private account directory. Have Hermes discover, install, run three DuckDB CSV jobs, and repeat while reusing the same installation. Verify artifact hashes and independently computed totals.

entries.name: Native R and pinned Rocker images over SSH
entries.upstream: Rscript and Rocker runtime images on the account's local Docker daemon
entries.reuse: Use the managed environment tools, trusted workspace manifests, Rscript and verified job receipts.
entries.build: Select native R when its version matches the lock. Otherwise prepare a digest-pinned Docker image and bind jobs to the observed environment ID.
entries.test: Have Hermes discover R availability, prepare the approved environment, and run the same CSV summary twice. Compare independent totals and confirm the same environment and separate native jobs.

entries.name: OpenSSH
entries.upstream: SSH client with approved host identity handling
entries.reuse: Use the system SSH client and existing authorized authentication and host-key policy.
entries.build: Implement a constrained worker profile for sites that permit direct execution. Pass typed recipe arguments, constrain working paths and persist the handoff before dispatch.
entries.test: Exercise a known host, host-key mismatch, permission denial and disconnect after dispatch. Reconcile the existing work without submitting it twice.

entries.name: OLDT Data Factory
entries.upstream: External-worker dispatch, HPC package generator and result import
entries.reuse: Reuse dispatch manifests, viewer-artifacts stage, portable inputs and existing result and artifact contracts.
entries.build: Bind the worker and MCP job IDs to the OLDT dispatch and revision. Return artifacts for explicit import and validation.
entries.test: Run the same permitted Guanajuato package locally and remotely. Check manifest, CRS, coverage, feature IDs, MVT/PMTiles/3D Tiles validity and successful opening in a test Twin.

entries.name: Local CPU reference runner
entries.upstream: Reviewed fixed local recipe and OS process lifecycle
entries.reuse: Reuse the same versioned program and input bundle used in the remote job.
entries.build: Create a tiny native reference and shared expected output. Preserve resource limits and a stable exit status in its lifecycle receipt.
entries.test: Verify exact synthetic results, nonzero exit handling and timeout. Compare with the first remote and MCP results.

entries.name: Slurm CLI
entries.upstream: sbatch, squeue, sacct, scancel and site QoS
entries.reuse: Reuse native scheduler, resource requests, accounting and cancellation semantics.
entries.build: Map typed resource requests and native states. Resolve cancellation through the registered request UUID and confirm the owned allocation in the queue.
entries.test: Check pending, success, failure, accounting retention and native versus MCP output. Verify that an agent cancels a running MPI allocation, then confirm native accounting, process shutdown, and rejection of an unknown UUID. Qualify job arrays separately.

entries.name: slurmrestd
entries.upstream: Versioned OpenAPI via a site-enabled Slurm REST service
entries.reuse: Reuse the site's authenticated REST entry point and advertised API version.
entries.build: Add conformance against the common job fields, preserving provider errors and version differences.
entries.test: Compare submit, query and cancel with the CLI on the same test cluster. Verify unavailable service, authorization refusal and unsupported schema.

entries.name: OpenPBS
entries.upstream: qsub, qstat and qdel
entries.reuse: Reuse PBS job scripts, resource syntax, arrays and lifecycle commands.
entries.build: Translate the typed job request into the existing OLDT PBS bundle and normalize state only where meanings match.
entries.test: Run a two-task job, retain per-task results, test rejection and cancellation, and compare PBS output with direct execution.

entries.name: HTCondor
entries.upstream: Python bindings and submit descriptions
entries.reuse: Reuse Schedd queries, native submit API and file-transfer features.
entries.build: Map independent scenario tasks and preserve the cluster and process identity for each output.
entries.test: Run an independently verifiable batch, force one job into a held state and compare job history and outputs with the native path.

entries.name: IBM Spectrum LSF
entries.upstream: bsub, bjobs and bkill at an approved installation
entries.reuse: Reuse the native queue and resource request syntax.
entries.build: Add a profile only for a confirmed site and inspect its licensed client and parsing interface.
entries.test: Check successful and rejected jobs and compare owner-scoped cancellation and accounting with direct LSF operation.

entries.name: Flux Framework
entries.upstream: Flux job CLI and Python API
entries.reuse: Reuse Flux resource and job abstractions at sites with a supported deployment.
entries.build: Map one allocation-scoped workload and keep nested job IDs and parent allocation visible.
entries.test: Run a job in a non-production Flux allocation and verify resources, completion and cancellation against the native receipt.

entries.name: CSC Slurm MCP
entries.upstream: Site-provided MCP for Slurm
entries.reuse: Inspect the actual tool contract and reuse bounded scheduler tools if the site offers a supported path.
entries.build: Add a profile and result-bundle translation only for required operations absent from the current tool contract.
entries.test: List tools, run a permitted fixture using native and MCP paths, compare results and test a disallowed operation in the authorized profile.

entries.name: Community HPC MCP
entries.upstream: Per-user Slurm and PBS MCP project
entries.reuse: Review the current license, tool list, scheduler-only configuration and versions.
entries.build: Use only the operations required by the project and keep shell and general file editing outside the integration profile.
entries.test: In an isolated lab review all exposed tools, then compare a fixed job with the native scheduler and verify the configured scope.

entries.name: FirecREST
entries.upstream: CSCS REST and client endpoints for jobs and transfer
entries.reuse: Use the site-provided authorization, scheduler and staged transfer APIs.
entries.build: Preserve remote job and transfer IDs in a shared receipt and map site-specific availability into discovery.
entries.test: Run a fixture with approved test data, compare the returned job record, verify checksums and handle token expiration and transfer failure.

entries.name: Globus Compute
entries.upstream: Compute endpoint and service API
entries.reuse: Use the institution's provisioned endpoint and task lifecycle where accepted.
entries.build: Register fixed compute functions or reviewed recipes through the existing endpoint and reconcile their task IDs.
entries.test: Submit an approved deterministic CPU fixture and exercise lost client connection, duplicate handling and expired credentials.

entries.name: Open OnDemand
entries.upstream: Institutional web portal and job tooling
entries.reuse: Use the site portal as a human reference for available queues and job states.
entries.build: Record the supported automation route offered by the site. Treat UI functions as operator references when a stable API is unavailable.
entries.test: Compare a test job view and accounting fields against the scheduler path with the same authorized account.

entries.name: SFTP
entries.upstream: OpenSSH file transfer
entries.reuse: Reuse authorized SFTP with separate input and output paths.
entries.build: Add a manifest for file IDs, bytes and hashes, transfer to a temporary name and publish a completed artifact only after verification.
entries.test: Interrupt a transfer, resume or retry via the supported mechanism, and reject a changed hash or out-of-scope target path.

entries.name: rsync
entries.upstream: SSH-backed incremental file synchronization
entries.reuse: Reuse the existing Data Factory transfer plans and native rsync features.
entries.build: Execute against configured source and destination roots and return a checked transfer receipt.
entries.test: Run initial and restart transfers on a test bundle, attempt an out-of-scope symlink, then verify exact output hashes.

entries.name: Globus Transfer
entries.upstream: Managed transfers between configured collections
entries.reuse: Use the existing task and monitoring API and supported checksum mode.
entries.build: Bind the two collection identities, transfer task and artifact checksums to the job receipt.
entries.test: Transfer a permitted test bundle, compare hashes, and exercise cancellation, authorization failure and retry.

entries.name: S3-compatible object storage
entries.upstream: Provider SDK and explicit artifact URIs
entries.reuse: Reuse a configured bucket, object versions and supported checksum metadata.
entries.build: Keep per-job prefixes and preserve exact version, size, content SHA-256 and expiry in the import manifest.
entries.test: Test upload, interrupted retrieval, object replacement and checksum rejection without relying on multipart ETags as content hashes.

entries.name: Docker Engine
entries.upstream: Images and controlled runtime configuration
entries.reuse: Reuse the permitted site runtime, with fixed images addressed by digest.
entries.build: Pin the command, mounts, CPU and memory settings at the worker boundary and separate logs from results.
entries.test: Run the same image twice, verify results and limits, and confirm that a disallowed mount or resource request is rejected upstream of submission.

entries.name: Apptainer
entries.upstream: SIF containers and site MPI integration
entries.reuse: Use the center-supported container execution and bind-mount policy.
entries.build: Add a compatible SIF build or approved digest reference and map launcher and MPI compatibility.
entries.test: Repeat a CPU fixture and two-rank MPI fixture under the authorized scheduler, checking image identity and portability.

entries.name: Environment Modules
entries.upstream: Site-defined modulefiles and versions
entries.reuse: Reuse the module stack provided at the institution.
entries.build: Record loaded modules and compiler/runtime versions in the job manifest.
entries.test: Rebuild a fixture in a clean job environment and show an unavailable module gives a clear failure rather than a fallback.

entries.name: Spack
entries.upstream: Locked scientific software environments
entries.reuse: Use a site-approved Spack environment, compiler and external dependency definitions.
entries.build: Store a recipe reference and lock-file digest, with compatibility rules for the chosen node.
entries.test: Build the same fixture from a fresh environment and compare runtime dependencies and outputs across two authorized targets.

entries.name: Open MPI
entries.upstream: MPI runtime and launcher
entries.reuse: Reuse Open MPI for process launch and communication within a Slurm allocation.
entries.build: Record ranks, allocated CPUs, rank affinity, transport and image versions. Leave scientific parallelization to the workload.
entries.test: Compare one, two and four ranks for a fixed periodic heat stencil on one node. Require identical field digests and agreement with the analytic solution, and record speedup separately for the kernel and launcher.

entries.name: LAMMPS
entries.upstream: Molecular dynamics executable and documented input format
entries.reuse: Run the packaged MPI executable and use its distributed force calculations and thermodynamic output.
entries.build: Stage hashed simulation inputs and recover thermodynamic samples and a restart file through the Slurm job contract. Expose bounded recipe parameters and let the agent read verified JSON results.
entries.test: Check fixed-volume copper dynamics across rank counts and across a checkpoint handoff. Have an agent run three initial temperatures from one recipe. Compare native thermodynamics and verify one Slurm allocation per UUID after a repeated submit.

entries.name: Nextflow
entries.upstream: Native workflow executors and run metadata
entries.reuse: Use versioned Nextflow pipelines and existing scheduler executors.
entries.build: Map pipeline parameters and final artifacts without reimplementing its DAG or task retry engine.
entries.test: Run a three-step synthetic workflow locally and on a test queue. Force one step to fail and verify restart and artifact identity.

entries.name: Snakemake
entries.upstream: Rules, workflow execution and Slurm executor plugin
entries.reuse: Reuse the original rules and supported executor plugin.
entries.build: Bind input assets, selected targets and output manifest to the MCP job request.
entries.test: Compare local and Slurm output hashes for a three-rule workflow, check missing input and resumption.

entries.name: Parsl
entries.upstream: Python workflow and execution providers
entries.reuse: Reuse the application's Python DAG and supported execution provider.
entries.build: Register versioned workflows and capture outputs and statuses at the recipe boundary.
entries.test: Run an independent-task workload, fail one task and verify final artifacts and failure scope with a direct Parsl run.

entries.name: Dask Jobqueue
entries.upstream: Native Dask cluster launchers for batch systems
entries.reuse: Reuse the application's Dask tasks and existing cluster factory.
entries.build: Add a scoped resource request for the scheduler and record worker counts, failure and cleanup.
entries.test: Compare a partitioned spatial summary to a serial reference and test a worker failure without losing the final job state.

entries.name: Ray Jobs
entries.upstream: Jobs API on a configured Ray deployment
entries.reuse: Reuse JobSubmissionClient and existing workload definitions.
entries.build: Bind Ray submission and logs to the common receipt and record which cluster provisioned the resources.
entries.test: Run a small parallel fixture, recover the receipt after client exit and confirm cancellation only affects the owned job.

entries.name: Kubernetes Jobs + Kueue
entries.upstream: Kubernetes Job API and Kueue admission and quotas
entries.reuse: Reuse Job and queue policies in an approved namespace.
entries.build: Map recipes to approved Job templates and keep the workload admission state distinct from execution.
entries.test: Check one admitted job, one job pending quota and one failed pod. Verify output access is scoped to the job namespace.

entries.name: AWS Batch
entries.upstream: Batch job definitions, queues, arrays and multi-node jobs
entries.reuse: Reuse official batch APIs and the selected job definition.
entries.build: Add identity for queue and job definition versions, permitted project and cost/capacity fields where available.
entries.test: Run a bounded CPU job and array in an authorized environment. Capture native IDs, failure reason, artifacts and observable billing units.

entries.name: Azure Batch
entries.upstream: Batch pools, jobs and tasks
entries.reuse: Reuse official Batch client and an approved pool.
entries.build: Map tasks and their children to per-job outputs and preserve pool sizing and start latency.
entries.test: Run a fixed task on an authorized pool, verify outputs and compare lifecycle after a failing task and client reconnection.

entries.name: Google Cloud Batch
entries.upstream: Jobs API, tasks and configured compute resources
entries.reuse: Reuse the existing Batch service and permitted storage identities.
entries.build: Map the native job and task groups into the project receipt and preserve region and resource profile.
entries.test: Run a bounded fixture with a fixed image, verify the output hash, handle quota rejection and reconcile the same job ID after reconnect.

entries.name: Slurm accounting and efficiency
entries.upstream: sacct and available site accounting data
entries.reuse: Use native elapsed, CPU and memory fields where available.
entries.build: Record units, observation scope and unavailable fields, keeping allocated resources distinct from consumption.
entries.test: Compare MCP metrics with native accounting for a short CPU job and check the missing-accounting case.

entries.name: NVIDIA DCGM Exporter
entries.upstream: DCGM metrics exposed to Prometheus
entries.reuse: Reuse site-approved GPU telemetry with access to authorized labels.
entries.build: Bind available samples to the job allocation, and represent shared-device and missing attribution accurately.
entries.test: Run a fixed GPU job where permitted, compare receipt times with telemetry, and record missing or shared metrics explicitly.

entries.name: Urban MCP SWMM
entries.upstream: Existing EPA SWMM and PySWMM case and observed rainfall fixtures
entries.reuse: Reuse the historical case, engine, inputs and permitted recipes.
entries.build: Make a typed parameter-sweep workload, preserving model baseline and one output per scenario.
entries.test: Compare all per-node rows against native independent runs within declared tolerances, test one failed task and measure batch overhead.

entries.name: Urban MCP SUMO
entries.upstream: Existing SUMO experiment, model and fixed seeds
entries.reuse: Reuse native models and outputs, including interrupted and incomplete trips.
entries.build: Schedule independent repetitions and aggregate them without changing per-trip meaning.
entries.test: Compare fixed-seed outputs with native single runs and preserve all trip, teleport and censor accounting when aggregating.

entries.name: CUDA-Q distributed simulation
entries.upstream: CUDA-Q distributed backends and MPI
entries.reuse: Use the simulation runtime and CUDA-aware infrastructure, with the Quantum circuit manifest as input.
entries.build: Bind circuit identity and simulator configuration to an HPC recipe and return measurements to Quantum.
entries.test: Check a known circuit locally and across the authorized MPI allocation. Compare probabilities within tolerance and report simulator configuration.

entries.name: Lmod
entries.upstream: Lua modulefiles and site environment hierarchy
entries.reuse: Reuse the active module hierarchy on the authorized cluster.
entries.build: Record exact modules and resolve environment dependencies through the site's normal startup path.
entries.test: Compare interactive discovery with a clean batch run, verify the same modules are loaded and report a missing dependency explicitly.

entries.name: OpenMP
entries.upstream: Threads and affinity settings in a compatible compiled workload
entries.reuse: Use the existing workload's OpenMP parallel regions.
entries.build: Bind the requested CPUs to explicit thread settings and record the observed environment.
entries.test: Compare a serial and threaded reference reduction, verify thread allocation and measure overhead without assuming speedup.

entries.name: DMTCP
entries.upstream: Checkpoint and restart for compatible Linux processes
entries.reuse: Reuse the workload's own checkpoint when available and evaluate DMTCP for a supported process.
entries.build: Associate checkpoint version, hash and compatible target scope with an explicit resume operation.
entries.test: Interrupt a permitted job, restore from its checkpoint and verify final results and restricted checkpoint access.

entries.name: IBM LSF quantum plugins
entries.upstream: Vendor-backed integration of LSF workload management and QPU dispatch
entries.reuse: Inspect existing plugin code, dependencies and target support at a site already authorized to use LSF and a quantum backend.
entries.build: Map the scheduler job and quantum execution IDs into linked receipts if the original tools expose both. Reuse the existing scheduler and provider queue.
entries.test: Run one fixed simulator-backed job first. In an authorized QPU experiment verify independent scheduler and device states, result provenance and the scope of cancellation.
